title: Coherent diagram of abelian stage sections
statement: Let J be a small category and F:J\to\mathrm{Cat} a diagram of small categories. Let P_j be a precoverage on F(j) [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with continuous transition functors for the generated topologies. Let V be a cocone of F [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and Q a precoverage on V.pt with each V_j continuous. Fix i in J and an abelian sheaf G on P_i. For t in Under(i), supply a map alpha_t from inverse image of G along F(t.hom) to restriction along V_t of its inverse image along V_i. For b:t\to t', supply theta_b from the inverse image along F(t.hom) to restriction along F(b.right) of the inverse image along F(t'.hom). Suppose the stage unit followed by alpha_t equals the V_i unit, and the stage unit followed by theta_b equals the t' unit, as equalities in the arrow category including endpoints [def-weil-pbc-arrows-functor]. Then for every U in F(i) there exist a diagram D:Under(i)\to\mathrm{Ab}, isomorphisms E_t from D(t) to the stage inverse-image sections at F(t.hom)(U), a cocone K of D and an isomorphism e from K.pt to the limit inverse-image sections at V_i(U). Each K leg followed by e equals E_t followed by alpha_t on sections, and E_t followed by theta_b on sections equals D(b) followed by E_t'. These are equalities in the arrow category. No filteredness, colimit or finite-cover assumption is required, and no colimit property of K is asserted.

proof.text: Injectivity of each stage adjunction hom equivalence shows that a map from the inverse image is determined by its composite with the unit. Equality of all section components is equality of sheaf maps. Apply this to the unit characterizations of theta and alpha. The identity theta is identity, consecutive theta maps compose to theta of the composite, and theta followed by restriction of the next alpha equals the previous alpha. To check composition, reassociate the composite with the first unit, replace it by the next unit, then use the next unit equation. Strict cocone and diagram equalities identify the composite restriction functors. This uses Mathlib adjunction homEquiv injectivity and apply_symm_apply directly; it does not invoke the separate conjugate-isomorphism theorem.

Set D(t) equal to stage inverse-image sections at F(t.hom)(U). Define D(b) by theta_b on sections followed by eqToHom transporting its target along F.map_comp and the under-category equation. The identity and composition equations above give the functor laws; naturality of theta along the object equality commutes the intermediate transport past the next theta.

Set K.pt equal to the limit inverse-image sections at V_i(U). Set its t leg to alpha_t on sections followed by eqToHom from cocone naturality. The theta-alpha equation and naturality of alpha commute the intermediate transport and give K naturality. Take E_t and e to be identity isomorphisms. The two arrow equalities follow by removing final eqToHom transports in the arrow category. Everything is constructed explicitly, and no object comes from a mere-existence theorem.

theorem colimit_site_abelian_section_diagram
    (J : Type u) [SmallCategory J] (F : J ⥤ Cat.{u, u})
    (P : ∀ j : J, Precoverage (F.obj j))
    [∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k),
      (F.map a).toFunctor.IsContinuous (P j).toGrothendieck (P k).toGrothendieck]
    (V : Cocone F) (Q : Precoverage V.pt)
    [∀ j : J, (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.IsContinuous
      (P j).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck]
    (i : J) (G : Sheaf (P i).toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (α : ∀ t : Under i,
      (sheafPullback (F.map t.hom).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P i).toGrothendieck (P
        t.right).toGrothendieck).obj G ⟶
      ((V.ι.app t.right).toFunctor.sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P
        t.right).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).obj
        ((sheafPullback (V.ι.app i).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P i).toGrothendieck
          Q.toGrothendieck).obj G))
    (θ : ∀ (t t' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t'),
      (sheafPullback (F.map t.hom).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P i).toGrothendieck (P
        t.right).toGrothendieck).obj G ⟶
      ((F.map b.right).toFunctor.sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P
        t.right).toGrothendieck (P t'.right).toGrothendieck).obj
        ((sheafPullback (F.map t'.hom).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P i).toGrothendieck (P
          t'.right).toGrothendieck).obj G))
    (hα : ∀ (t : Under i) (X : F.obj i),
      Arrow.mk (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (F.map t.hom).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P
        i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).unit.app G).hom.app (op X) ≫ (α t).hom.app
        (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj X))) =
      Arrow.mk (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (V.ι.app i).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P
        i).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).unit.app G).hom.app (op X)))
    (hθ : ∀ (t t' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t') (X : F.obj i),
      Arrow.mk (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (F.map t.hom).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P
        i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).unit.app G).hom.app (op X) ≫
        (θ t t' b).hom.app (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj X))) =
      Arrow.mk (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (F.map t'.hom).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P
        i).toGrothendieck (P t'.right).toGrothendieck).unit.app G).hom.app (op X)))
    (U : F.obj i) :
    ∃ (D : Under i ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u})
      (E : ∀ t : Under i, D.obj t ≅
      ((sheafPullback (F.map t.hom).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P i).toGrothendieck (P
        t.right).toGrothendieck).obj G).obj.obj (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj U))) (K : Cocone
        D) (e : K.pt ≅ ((sheafPullback (V.ι.app i).toFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (P
        i).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).obj G).obj.obj (op ((V.ι.app i).toFunctor.obj U))),
      (∀ t : Under i, Arrow.mk (K.ι.app t ≫ e.hom) =
      Arrow.mk ((E t).hom ≫ (α t).hom.app (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj U)))) ∧ (∀ (t t' :
        Under i) (b : t ⟶ t'),
      Arrow.mk ((E t).hom ≫ (θ t t' b).hom.app (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj U))) =
      Arrow.mk (D.map b ≫ (E t').hom))
